cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell: one third-party path (jansson 2.15.1, 282,984 Debian popcon sourcemax installations, captured 2026-11-17) was built, control-verified against the exact nested structure of the control, and given native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'json' (24 hits, 3 of them C JSON parsers) plus three targeted C names (jansson, jsmn, parson); adoption was compared with Debian popcon sourcemax counts. json-c (269,736) is within 5% of jansson and was not built; cJSON (150,958) and yyjson (14,868) were not built. Popcon counts Debian installations of the library packages, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not developer choice; parson has no Debian package and no comparable number. Conan and Debian do not cover vendored single-file copies (common for cJSON). ISO C documents no JSON API. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

cells.selection: mpg123 has the highest Homebrew install-on-request count (12,256) among hits whose own C library decodes MPEG Layer III frames from a documented byte API. lame (6,992) ranks next but its HIP decoder is built over libmpg123.
cells.uncertainty: One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad is an unresolved independent family. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for the whole mpg123 distribution (player and library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: one third-party path (stream-json 3.9.0, 56,997,988 npm downloads 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-15) was built, control-verified, and given parser-derived V8 AFL++ feedback. It is the highest-download lead found with its own RFC 8259 tokenizer and a documented local Buffer/stream API. jsonparse (105,362,611) has its own Buffer parser but no documented API and was not selected; json5, jsonc-parser, and json-bigint have higher downloads but string-only APIs and/or superset grammars. Six high-download packages delegate to JSON.parse. Downloads were fetched for 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. The standard JSON.parse path is counted separately; V8 parses it natively, so it has a control receipt but no parser source lines or AFL++ feedback. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: one third-party path (saxes 6.0.0, 601,886,067 npm downloads 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-15) was built, verified on two valid namespace controls against the expat oracle, and given parser-derived V8 AFL++ feedback. It is the highest-download lead in the snapshot with its own JavaScript XML 1.0 + Namespaces parser and namespace URI resolution; jsdom (587,846,374) delegates its XML parsing to saxes, and htmlparser2 (526,964,241) is an HTML tokenizer with an xmlMode. sax (490,225,823), fast-xml-parser (426,764,010) and @xmldom/xmldom (326,406,305) have their own parsers and were not run. Downloads were fetched for 19 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit; transitive dependency downloads (jsdom pulls saxes) inflate saxes's count relative to direct use. saxes takes strings, so the adapter decodes bytes with a strict UTF-8 TextDecoder first. Node.js 26.10.0 core has no XML parser API, so the standard count is 0. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value normalization behaviour.
